question: Should `gateway.controlUi.allowedOrigins` accept scheme-level wildcard entries such as `chrome-extension://*`, and if so what schemes and wildcard grammar are acceptable for Gateway browser-origin authorization?
rationale: This changes a browser-origin authorization boundary and the current documented config contract only supports full-origin entries plus the global `*`.

options.title: Approve constrained extension wildcard grammar
options.body: Define an explicit extension-scheme-only grammar, add shared matcher coverage, and document the allow/reject cases before implementation.

options.title: Keep exact origins only
options.body: Reject scheme wildcards and rely on exact opaque-origin fixes plus the existing global `*` escape hatch for deliberately broad local testing.

options.title: Fold into broader pattern contract
options.body: Wait for the loopback pattern work to settle and decide whether Chrome extension wildcards belong in the same public config contract or a separate one.

recommendation.title: Approve constrained extension wildcard grammar
recommendation.body: Define an explicit extension-scheme-only grammar, add shared matcher coverage, and document the allow/reject cases before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest history on the Gateway origin-check boundary and explicit non-loopback origin policy.
